themes_detail.label: Unleashed dogs surge
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—an 700% increase (z-score: 4.95)—signaling a sudden public safety and park access concern in East Harlem.
evidence: 4 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
Statistically anomalous spike emerged in the most recent reporting period
Community board has standing requests for park improvements, suggesting existing park pressure
reporting_angles: Interview residents and dog owners in major parks (Marcus Garvey, Jefferson, Harlem Meer) about the uptick and enforcement visibility
Check with Parks Enforcement Patrol on staffing levels and citation trends this week

themes_detail.label: Vehicle noise complaints double
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints hit 36 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 269% increase from the 9.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.34), aligning with community board requests for additional traffic enforcement agents and suggesting a sustained street-level disturbance problem.
evidence: 36 vehicle noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 9.8 weekly average (269% spike, z-score: 5.34)
Community board has filed repeated budget requests to 'Hire additional traffic enforcement agents' (NYPD)
Unsolved, long-standing concern suggests structural enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Ride-along with traffic enforcement agents to document vehicle noise violation patterns and enforcement capacity
Interview residents on 125th Street and major avenues about noise intensity and times of day; cross-reference with NYPD complaint data

themes_detail.label: Park rule violations spike
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints surged to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1500% increase from the 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.66), suggesting a sudden shift in park use, enforcement, or community reporting that warrants rapid investigation.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
Overlaps with unleashed dog spike and litter basket requests, suggesting park ecosystem stress
Community board has standing requests for park improvements and access enhancements
reporting_angles: Survey major East Harlem parks (Marcus Garvey, Jefferson, Harlem Meer) to document violations: drinking, dog control, vandalism, etc.
Interview Parks Enforcement Patrol supervisor on what rule violations were cited and whether staffing or patrol patterns changed 2+ weeks ago

themes_detail.label: Obstruction complaints rise sharply
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 336% increase from the 1.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.4), indicating sidewalk or public-space blockages that may reflect construction, vendor encroachment, or parking violations affecting pedestrian mobility.
evidence: 6 obstruction complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly average (336% spike, z-score: 5.4)
Community board requests for street and sidewalk improvements, plus traffic enforcement agents
566 building permits filed in last 90 days (470 alterations) may be generating street-level construction obstruction
reporting_angles: Walk major corridors (125th Street, Park Ave, Madison Ave) to document obstructions: construction debris, vendor tables, parked vehicles, scaffolding
Check DOB permit database for active alteration projects with street impact; cross-reference with 311 complaint addresses

themes_detail.label: Cannabis retailer complaints cluster
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints reached 9 THREE WEEKS AGO, a 454% increase from the 1.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.68), suggesting either a wave of new unlicensed retailers opening or community friction over legal cannabis operations.
evidence: 9 cannabis retailer complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.6 weekly average (454% spike, z-score: 4.68)
Spike is 3 weeks old; does not appear to be sustained at elevated levels in most recent week
May reflect community push-back on unlicensed retailers or odor/behavior complaints at legal shops
reporting_angles: Map the 9 complaints spatially; determine if they cluster on a single block or corridor (licensed vs. unlicensed establishments)
Interview SLA (State Liquor Authority) and OCME (Office of Cannabis Management) on enforcement activity and licensed retail locations in CD 111 over the past month
